clauses.title: Record retention and data availability obligations
clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that vendor contracts require the retention of customer identification, transaction and monitoring records for at least the period set in the bank's retention schedule. The vendor shall store records securely, keep them retrievable within an agreed time and provide them to the bank on request in a readable form. On expiry or termination, the vendor shall return or transfer all records to the bank and shall destroy remaining copies only on the bank's written instruction.

clauses.title: Termination rights for compliance failures
clauses.text: The bank shall include in each vendor contract a right to suspend or terminate the arrangement, without penalty to the bank, where the vendor materially breaches its financial-crime obligations, fails to remediate audit findings on time, or becomes subject to a sanctions designation or serious enforcement action. The contract shall provide for an orderly transition so that controls continue to operate during exit. The bank shall document the trigger events and maintain a tested exit plan for critical vendors.

clauses.title: Product owner accountability for launch risk assessment
clauses.text: The bank shall require the accountable product owner to complete a documented financial crime risk assessment before any new product is submitted for approval. The assessment shall describe the intended customers, the delivery channels, the geographies served and the expected transaction behaviour. The product owner shall personally attest that the assessment is accurate and complete, and no launch request shall proceed without that attestation.

clauses.title: Independent compliance review before approval
clauses.text: The bank shall ensure that every launch request receives an independent review by the financial crime compliance function before final approval. The reviewer shall be free of commercial targets tied to the product, shall challenge the stated risk ratings, and shall record a clear recommendation to approve, approve with conditions, or decline. The business shall not override a decline recommendation without escalation to the designated senior risk committee.

clauses.title: Conditional approvals and remediation deadlines
clauses.text: Where the bank grants approval subject to conditions, the bank shall state each condition in writing, assign a named owner and set a firm completion date. Conditions that address control gaps shall be closed before launch unless the senior risk committee accepts a documented interim measure. The bank shall track open conditions to closure and shall suspend further rollout where a deadline is missed without an approved extension.

clauses.title: Sign-off for material changes to live products
clauses.text: The bank shall treat a material change to a live product as requiring fresh sign-off, even when the original launch was approved. Material changes include new features, altered transaction limits, new customer segments, additional delivery channels and changes to supporting processes. The product owner shall submit a change assessment, and the compliance function shall decide whether a full or abbreviated review is needed before the change goes live.

clauses.title: Retention of sign-off evidence and periodic reattestation
clauses.text: The bank shall retain all sign-off records, including assessments, review notes, conditions and final decisions, in a central repository that is accessible to audit and regulators on request. Product owners shall reattest to the continued accuracy of each assessment at least annually. Where the attestation cannot be given, the owner shall notify the compliance function, which shall decide whether the product must be reviewed again.

clauses.title: Setting launch limits for new products
clauses.text: The bank shall define transaction, daily, and balance limits for every new product before launch, based on the product's inherent risk assessment and the expected behaviour of its target customers. Limits shall be documented with a written rationale, approved by the product owner and the financial crime risk function, and configured in the system of record. No product shall go live with unlimited or undefined thresholds.

clauses.title: Velocity thresholds for rapid fund movement
clauses.text: The bank shall configure velocity thresholds that measure the number and value of incoming and outgoing transfers over defined rolling periods, including short windows of hours and days. Products that allow funds to be received and sent onward quickly shall carry tighter thresholds. Breaches shall generate alerts for review, and the thresholds shall be tested before any change to transfer speed or payment features is released.

clauses.title: Controls on customer limit increase requests
clauses.text: The bank shall treat every request to raise a customer's limits as a risk event. Before approving an increase, the bank shall confirm the customer's identity, review account activity and source of funds against the stated purpose, and consider adverse information. Increases for higher-risk customers shall require enhanced review and senior approval, and each decision shall be recorded with its justification.

clauses.title: Lower limits for higher-risk geographies
clauses.text: The bank shall apply reduced transaction and velocity limits to payments involving countries or corridors rated higher risk under the bank's geographic risk methodology. Before the bank enters a new geography, it shall set corridor-specific limits and review them after the first months of live activity. Limits shall not be relaxed for a corridor without documented approval from the financial crime risk function.

clauses.title: Limit recalibration and override governance
clauses.text: The bank shall review the effectiveness of limits and velocity thresholds at least annually, and after any material change in product design, channel, or customer mix, using alert volumes, investigation outcomes, and observed behaviour. Manual overrides of limits shall be exceptional, time-bound, and approved by an authorised officer. All overrides shall be logged and reported periodically to risk governance for oversight.

clauses.title: Disclosure of Product Limits and Restrictions
clauses.text: The bank shall disclose to customers, before account opening or first use, the transaction limits, eligibility conditions and permitted uses that apply to each product. Product owners shall document these restrictions in plain language and confirm that the disclosures match the controls configured in the systems. Any product launched without reviewed disclosures of its financial-crime-related restrictions shall not be released to customers until Compliance has approved the wording.

clauses.title: Corridor-Specific Disclosure for Cross-Border Transfers
clauses.text: The bank shall give customers clear disclosure of the destination corridors, additional verification steps, expected processing delays and possible holds that apply to cross-border transfers. Where a corridor carries elevated risk, the disclosure shall state that extra information about the sender, recipient or purpose may be requested. Product owners shall review corridor disclosures whenever a new destination is added or an existing corridor's risk rating changes.

clauses.title: Customer Notice of Monitoring and Reporting
clauses.text: The bank shall inform customers in its account terms that activity is monitored for financial-crime purposes and that information may be shared with competent authorities where required by law. Notices shall be worded generally and shall never reveal whether a specific customer is the subject of an alert, review or report. Staff shall use approved scripts when customers ask about monitoring, so that no inappropriate detail is disclosed.

clauses.title: Notification of Material Changes to Product Terms
clauses.text: The bank shall notify affected customers in advance of any material change to product terms that alters limits, verification requirements, permitted activity or the conditions for account restriction. Product owners shall assess each change for financial-crime impact before the notice is issued and keep a record of the assessment, the approved wording and the date customers were notified. Urgent changes made for risk reasons shall be explained as soon as practicable afterwards.

clauses.title: Consistency of Partner-Facing Customer Disclosures
clauses.text: The bank shall require any vendor or partner that presents the bank's products to customers to use disclosures that are consistent with the bank's approved wording on restrictions, verification and monitoring. Before onboarding, the business owner shall review the partner's customer-facing screens, scripts and documents across every channel. Agreements shall oblige the partner to obtain approval before changing those materials and to supply evidence of the versions in use on request.

clauses.title: Identity verification before account opening
clauses.text: The bank shall collect and verify identifying information for every prospective customer before an account is opened or a product is activated. Verification shall rely on documentary or non-documentary evidence from reliable, independent sources, and the method used shall be recorded in the customer file. Where identity cannot be verified within the defined period, the bank shall restrict activity, escalate to compliance, and decline or close the relationship if doubts remain unresolved.

clauses.title: Beneficial ownership of legal entity customers
clauses.text: The bank shall identify and verify the natural persons who ultimately own or control each legal entity customer, including those holding significant ownership and at least one individual with managerial control. Ownership structures involving trusts, nominees, bearer instruments or multiple layers shall be documented in a structure chart. Where beneficial owners cannot be established with confidence, the bank shall not onboard the entity without senior compliance approval and a written rationale.

clauses.title: Customer risk rating methodology at onboarding
clauses.text: The bank shall assign every customer an initial risk rating at onboarding, using a documented methodology that weighs customer type, expected products and services, delivery channel, and geographic exposure. Ratings shall be reproducible and recorded with the factors that drove them. Analysts may override a calculated rating only upward without approval, and any downward override shall require documented justification and review by a second qualified reviewer.

clauses.title: Enhanced due diligence for higher-risk relationships
clauses.text: The bank shall apply enhanced due diligence to customers rated high risk, including politically exposed persons, their close associates and family members, and customers with complex or opaque structures. Enhanced measures shall include corroborating source of wealth and source of funds, obtaining senior management approval before establishing the relationship, and applying closer ongoing monitoring. The reasons for accepting each such relationship shall be documented and retained in the customer file.

clauses.title: Periodic review and event-driven refresh of CDD
clauses.text: The bank shall keep customer due diligence information current through scheduled reviews whose frequency reflects the customer risk rating, and through event-driven refreshes. Triggering events include a material change in ownership, unexpected transaction patterns, adverse media, or a request for a new product. Reviews shall confirm that identification data, business purpose and expected activity remain accurate, and unresolved gaps shall lead to restrictions or exit decisions.

clauses.title: Use of third parties in identity verification
clauses.text: The bank shall perform documented due diligence on any vendor or third party that supports customer identification or verification, including digital identity providers, before reliance begins. Contracts shall define data quality standards, audit rights, record access and incident notification. The bank remains accountable for verification outcomes, shall test vendor accuracy on a sample basis at least annually, and shall suspend reliance where performance falls below the agreed thresholds.

clauses.title: PEP screening at onboarding
clauses.text: The bank shall screen every prospective customer, and every natural person connected to a prospective legal entity customer, against its approved politically exposed person data before an account is opened. Screening shall cover domestic, foreign and international organisation roles. Potential matches shall be reviewed by a trained analyst, who shall record the reasoning for confirming or discarding each match. No account shall be activated while a potential match remains unresolved.

clauses.title: Family members and close associates of PEPs
clauses.text: The bank shall extend its politically exposed person controls to immediate family members and known close associates of a confirmed public official. Relationship staff shall ask onboarding questions designed to reveal such links, including shared business interests and joint ownership. Where a link is identified, the customer shall be treated as a politically exposed relationship for risk rating, and the basis for that treatment shall be documented in the customer file.

clauses.title: Identifying beneficial owners of entities
clauses.text: The bank shall identify and verify each individual who ultimately owns a defined percentage of a legal entity customer, together with at least one individual who exercises effective control over it. The ownership percentage applied shall be set out in the bank's procedures and reviewed annually. Where no individual meets the ownership test, the bank shall rely on the control individual and record why no owner was identified.

clauses.title: Layered ownership and nominee arrangements
clauses.text: The bank shall look through multi-layer ownership structures until the natural persons who ultimately own or control the customer are established. Structures that involve nominee shareholders, bearer instruments, trusts or holding companies in secrecy-oriented territories shall be escalated for enhanced review. Onboarding staff shall obtain a structure chart and supporting documents, and shall decline the relationship if the real controllers cannot be reliably established.

clauses.title: Senior approval and refresh for PEP relationships
clauses.text: The bank shall require written approval from a designated senior compliance officer before onboarding or retaining any customer confirmed as a politically exposed person or as having such a beneficial owner. The approval shall record the source of wealth and source of funds. These relationships shall receive enhanced ongoing monitoring and a full file refresh at least annually, or sooner when a trigger event occurs.

clauses.title: Risk-Tiered Refresh Cadence for Customer Records
clauses.text: The bank shall refresh customer due diligence records on a cycle set by the customer's assigned risk tier. Higher-risk customers shall be reviewed more often than standard-risk customers, and low-risk customers shall be reviewed on the longest permitted cycle. Each refresh shall confirm identity details, the stated purpose of the relationship, expected activity, and the current risk rating. Business owners shall record the completion date and the reviewer, and overdue reviews shall be reported to the control function monthly.

clauses.title: Event-Driven Refresh Outside the Normal Cycle
clauses.text: The bank shall start an unscheduled refresh whenever a material event suggests that the existing customer profile may no longer be accurate. Such events include a sudden change in transaction patterns, adverse media about the customer, a change of name or address to a higher-risk location, a new product request, or an internal escalation from investigations staff. The refresh shall begin within a defined number of business days, and its outcome shall be documented and may change the customer's risk rating.

clauses.title: Re-Verifying Ownership and Control of Entity Customers
clauses.text: For legal entity customers, the bank shall re-verify the beneficial owners and the individuals who exercise control at each scheduled refresh. Relationship managers shall obtain a current ownership statement, compare it with the records held, and investigate any unexplained change in structure, such as a new intermediate holding company or a transfer of significant shares. Where ownership cannot be traced to natural persons, the case shall be escalated to compliance before the refresh can be closed.

clauses.title: Handling Customers Who Do Not Respond to Refresh
clauses.text: The bank shall apply a staged escalation when a customer fails to respond to a refresh request. After the first missed deadline the bank shall send a reminder through an alternate contact method. If the customer remains unresponsive, the bank shall place reasonable limits on new products and services. Continued non-response shall lead to a documented decision on restricting or exiting the relationship, and compliance shall decide whether any unusual activity report is warranted before the account is closed.

clauses.title: Business owner attestation before segment launch
clauses.text: The bank shall require the accountable business owner to sign a written segment attestation before any new customer segment is opened for onboarding. The attestation shall confirm that the segment's inherent financial-crime risks have been assessed, that onboarding procedures are matched to those risks, and that staffing and monitoring capacity are sufficient. No account shall be opened for the segment until the attestation is recorded and acknowledged by Compliance.

clauses.title: Expected activity profile attestation
clauses.text: The bank shall require each segment attestation to state the expected activity profile for the segment, including typical transaction types, value ranges, volumes and counterparties. Relationship managers shall confirm that the profile reflects the actual customers being onboarded and not a generic template. Where observed activity departs materially from the attested profile, the bank shall escalate the variance for review and may require the attestation to be reissued.

clauses.title: Ownership and control attestation for entities
clauses.text: The bank shall require that, for any segment consisting of legal entities, the attestation confirms the method used to identify owners and controllers and the way their identities are verified. The business shall state which ownership structures fall outside the segment, such as layered or bearer-share arrangements, and shall direct those applicants to enhanced due diligence instead of standard onboarding.

clauses.title: Attestation renewal and material change triggers
clauses.text: The bank shall renew every segment attestation at least once a year and whenever a material change occurs. Material changes include a new product offered to the segment, a new feature that alters how funds move, a change in onboarding process, or expansion into a new country. An attestation that has lapsed shall suspend new onboarding into the segment until it is renewed and approved.

clauses.title: Vendor-assisted onboarding attestation and challenge
clauses.text: The bank shall require a supplementary attestation whenever a third-party vendor performs any part of onboarding for a segment. The attestation shall describe which checks the vendor performs, how the bank tests the vendor's output, and how exceptions are returned to the bank. The second line shall independently challenge the attestation and record its conclusions before the vendor is permitted to process live applications.
